title: Cross-validate: position SenML parity across impls
description: Verify Python/Rust/Zephyr produce identical SenML encoding
notes: STATUS: Python<->Rust byte-parity PROVEN and deviations FIXED; Zephyr C side BLOCKED (see notes). Rust fixes: (1) pos.rs lat/lon records used u="deg" instead of u="lat"/"lon" (spec appendix-senml F.3; new SENML_LOCATION_UNIT_LAT/UNIT_LON constants in lichen-core). (2) bt was always 9-byte 0xfb f64 while oracle/python emit shortest-form int (0x1a66536a90); new canonical codec rust/lichen-senml/src/wire.rs (encode+decode) reusing senml-cbor Record/CborError. NOTE: upstream senml-cbor cbor::decode cannot parse 4/8-byte int args (dec_head caps info<=25), i.e. it rejected the committed oracle bytes AND any Python-produced position pack - wire::decode replaces it on all Position decode paths. wire::decode enforces RFC8428 one-value-field rule (vector err-multiple-value-fields was silently accepted before); fixed skip_depth major-7 sizing bug (must use head size, not argument value). (3) Position::to_senml_cbor now rejects NaN/Inf + lat/[-90,90] + lon/[-180,180] matching python profiles.location and C senml_encode_location*. Tests: rust/lichen-client/tests/position_senml_vectors.rs (Position-level, all 12 vectors) + rust/lichen-senml/tests/location_vectors.rs (codec-level, incl oracle->re-encode stability) + 23 inline unit tests; oracle = test/vectors/senml_location.json (never code-under-test). All cargo tests green (lichen-senml 21+2+6, lichen-client 75+4+, lichen-core 300+), clippy clean, fmt applied; pytest senml_location_vectors+senml_resources 46 passed. ZEPHYR BLOCKERS in lichen/subsys/lichen/senml/senml.c (cannot build/test on macOS host; needs EC2 zephyr builder): a) duplicate definition of senml_encode_location_full (~L402 and ~L545) -> compile error; b) zcbor_float32_put emits 0xfa f32 values vs oracle 0xfb f64 (byte-parity break vs python/rust); c) encode order BT-before-BN contradicts oracle (a2 21(bn)..22(bt)) and its own 'canonical CBOR ordering' comment (deterministic CBOR sorts 0x21<0x22 => bn first); d) C uses float (f32) throughout so e.g. 37.774929f != f64 bits of oracle.
